title: Perfect projection formula for reductions
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be schemes, $f:X\to Y$ a morphism, and $(A,I)$ the adic datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $A$ commutative Noetherian, $P_n=A/I^n$ finite as a set and perfect in $D(A)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ and use the ordinary, uncompleted derived categories of $A_T$-module sheaves. The coefficient identification $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ is the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]; use the operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and their K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Fix $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The full isomorphism locus of the map $\pi_{f,K,P}$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], for $P\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, is a thick triangulated subcategory containing every finite free coefficient sheaf $A_Y^{\oplus m}$. It contains every site-perfect complex [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]: here site-perfect means locally on the site isomorphic to a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free coefficient sheaves, with bounds allowed to depend on the covering object. For every $n\geq1$ the canonical pullback comparison $Lf^*(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$ identifies the projection map with an isomorphism
$$\pi_n:(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n,\qquad K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_X}(P_n)_X.$$
Its inverse $\rho_n$ agrees with the signed-totalization inverse for a finite-projective resolution of $P_n$. These maps and inverses are independent of the chosen resolution and commute with quotient tower maps, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base change in the projection-formula square of [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-base-change-naturality]. For proper $f$, they also agree with the identity-compactification formula [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-identity-compactification].

proof.text: The profinite coefficient comparison gives the specified coefficient-ring identification. Apply native pro-etale projection-mate exactness to obtain the two exact functors and a shift-compatible natural transformation whose components are the actual projection maps. Its isomorphism locus is exactly locus. The existing NatTrans.isoLocus instances make that locus triangulated and stable under retracts.

The native exactness lemma gives invertibility at the degree-zero coefficient unit. Exactness of the two functors implies that the isomorphism locus is stable under finite products. Apply it to the limit cone of the finite discrete diagram of copies of the unit, preserved by the degree-zero single functor; this includes the empty product at rank zero.

proof.text: Open the definition of site-perfectness. For every site object choose its covering sieve and the bounded finite-free-retract model B on each covering object U. Use the actual native slice presentation to identify restriction of the projection mate with a shift-compatible natural transformation between exact slice functors. Restriction of the coefficient unit is the slice coefficient unit, so cancellation of the presentation comparisons gives its invertibility there. Finite products and retract closure put each term of B in its isomorphism locus; bounded-complex triangulated devissage puts Q(B) there. Transport along the local quasi-isomorphism and the chosen global model, then cancel the source and target comparison isomorphisms. Local detection of derived isomorphisms proves invertibility globally. Bounds and ranks may vary with U.

proof.text: For $P_n$, the perfect-ring definition and completed-constant reduction give a bounded finite-free-retract $A_T$-model of $(P_n)_T$. Step 3 applies. The equation $\pi_{X,n}c_f=c_{f,n}f^{-1}\pi_{Y,n}$ makes $c_{f,n}$ coefficient-linear; the operations have exact identified-coefficient pullback. Thus $Lf^*(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$. The ordinary quotient pullback uses the existing ring-restriction mate and adjunct equations, specialized only after a generic restricted-unit proof.

Apply the existing native SignedProjectionResolution.normalization theorem, using both its forward formula and its inverse identity. The proved normalization_with_coefficient_iso helper conjugates its target by the quotient-pullback tensor isomorphism over arbitrary coefficient sheaves, using only isomorphism cancellation. Specialize to the completed rings and the supplied representatives. Resolution.sourceModel and targetModel reuse the existing signed comparison constructors; Resolution.total and totalInverse reuse the existing signed chain maps. Their mathematical values are unchanged. The forward equation is the first conjunct. Since reductionMap is invertible by step 4, cancel it in the signed inverse identity to obtain the reverse equation. This proves resolution independence. The now-unused duplicate mixed, ordinary-unit, flatness, K-injectivity and push-model declarations of this item are pruned; the native theorems supplying them remain proved.

Stacks Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, is the counit-mate source.

proof.text: Naturality of the derived tensor and quotient coefficient maps proves the tower and operator squares. Prove coefficientMap_comp by uniqueness of the completed finite-quotient cone. The ordinary adjunction unit characterizations and the existing constant-comparison composition theorem, transposed by the abstract adjunction-composition identity, prove quotientPullback_compositor, and a generic derived degree-zero compositor lemma proves quotientDerivedPullback_compositor. These give the coefficient square. Combine the existing projection base-change equation with tensor naturality and that coefficient square; reduction_square_algebra carries out the associativity calculation. Since both forward projection maps are invertible, cancel them to obtain the inverse square without inverting the exchange map.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every $n$ there is a natural isomorphism

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n
\xrightarrow[\pi_n]{\sim}Rf_*K_n
$$

whose inverse is $\rho_n$. The families $(\pi_n)$ and $(\rho_n)$ commute
with the reduction tower, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base
change.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Choose a strict-perfect package $F_n^\bullet\to P_n$. Signed totalization
gives inverse arrows

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LF_n^\bullet
\mathrel{\substack{\xrightarrow{\ \pi_n\ }\\[-2pt]
\xleftarrow[\ \rho_n\ ]{}}}
Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*F_n^\bullet).
$$

Because $P_n$ is constant, $Lf^*P_n=P_n$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.
The identity-compactification lemma shows that this is also the open/proper
compactification composite for proper $f$. The totalization lemma gives
$\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Uniqueness of an inverse makes the map
independent of the strict-perfect package. Tower, operator, and base-change
compatibility are exactly the preceding two lemmas. This expands the
finite-projective argument located at Tag `0944`.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism. For
fixed $K\in D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$, the full subcategory of objects
$P\in D(Y_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ for which $\pi_{f,K,P}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is an isomorphism is a thick
triangulated subcategory containing every finite free $\Lambda_Y$-module. In
particular, it contains every perfect complex of $\Lambda_Y$-modules.

For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and $n\geq1$, the quotient
$P_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$ has the two-term resolution
$[\mathcal O_{E,Y}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,Y}]$
([det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]) and $Lf^*P_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$.
Writing $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, there is a
natural isomorphism

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,Y}}P_n
\xrightarrow[\pi_n]{\sim}Rf_*K_n
$$

whose inverse is $\rho_n$. The families $(\pi_n)$ and $(\rho_n)$ commute
with the reduction tower, compatible coefficient endomorphisms, and base
change.

proof.text:
For $P=\Lambda_Y$ the map $\pi_{f,K,\Lambda_Y}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map] is the canonical tensor identity, an
isomorphism; for a finite free $P=\Lambda_Y^m$ it is the direct sum of finitely
many of these, so every finite free $\Lambda_Y$-module lies in the full
subcategory. The
subcategory is triangulated-thick: it is closed under shifts ($Lf^*$, $Rf_*$
and tensor are exact triangulated by
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and commute with the shift comparisons),
under cones (applying $u:P_1\to P_2$ to the projection-formula maps makes the
cones of the $\pi$'s fit into a distinguished triangle, and the
two-out-of-three property gives the claim), and under direct summands (an
idempotent splitting of $P$ gives one of the isomorphism). Hence it contains
every perfect complex, i.e. every object of the thick triangulated
subcategory generated by the finite free modules. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$
this includes $P_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_Y$, by its two-term finite free
resolution ([det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]), giving the displayed
isomorphism $(Rf_*K)\otimes^LP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*K_n$.

Choose a strict-perfect package $F_n^\bullet\to P_n$. Signed totalization
gives inverse arrows

$$
(Rf_*K)\otimes^LF_n^\bullet
\mathrel{\substack{\xrightarrow{\ \pi_n\ }\\[-2pt]
\xleftarrow[\ \rho_n\ ]{}}}
Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*F_n^\bullet).
$$

Because $P_n$ is pulled back from the point, $Lf^*P_n=f^*p_Y^*(\mathcal
O_E/\pi_E^n)=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, and the target is $Rf_*K_n$.
The identity-compactification lemma shows that this is also the open/proper
compactification composite for proper $f$. The totalization lemma gives
$\rho_n\pi_n=1$ and $\pi_n\rho_n=1$. Uniqueness of an inverse makes the map
independent of the strict-perfect package. Tower, operator, and base-change
compatibility are exactly the preceding two lemmas. This expands the
finite-projective argument located at Tag `0944`.
